purpose: Expose the distinct information route, retained state or token geometry without copying report artwork
alt: Four ways to retain or read the past. Explicit history: Store keys and values by position. GQA reduces the number of KV heads, not the number of retained positions. Compressed history: MLA retains a compact content latent plus a positional key for each token. The history still grows. Selected reads: An indexer selects tokens or blocks before the main attention operation. Unselected history may still occupy storage. Recurrent state: Update a fixed-shape state instead of appending one record per token. Earlier details must survive compression.
caption: Figure 1. Retaining history and reading history are different decisions. Original synthesis; cells and selected rows are illustrative.

purpose: Expose the distinct information route, retained state or token geometry without copying report artwork
alt: Which representations reach the next computation?. Ordinary residual: One stream bypasses a sublayer and adds its update. Normalization placement is a separate choice. Constrained multiple streams: Read from several streams, compute one sublayer update, then mix the bypass and distribute the update. mHC constrains bypass mixing. Attention across depth: A learned query weights earlier representations or block summaries for the next sublayer. These sources are layers, not earlier sequence positions. Gated reads and writes: Read gates combine residual branches into a sublayer input; write gates distribute its update. Qwen3.8-Next does not use unrestricted branch-to-branch mixing.
caption: Figure 1. Accumulate, mix streams, attend across depth, or gate reads and writes. Independent mechanism comparison; normalization and full model details are omitted.

purpose: Expose the distinct information route, retained state or token geometry without copying report artwork
alt: Four interfaces with different jobs. CLIP · match representations: Separate image and text encoders produce comparable representations. CLIP alone is not a generative language decoder. BLIP-2 · query the image: Learned queries read vision features. Projected query outputs become visual prompts during generative pretraining. LLaVA · project the features: A connector maps image features into the language embedding space. Original LLaVA uses a linear projection; 1.5 uses an MLP. Qwen3-VL · add depth routes: Merged visual tokens enter the input; selected intermediate vision features also enter early decoder layers through DeepStack.
caption: Figure 1. Matching images and text is different from conditioning a language decoder. Independent comparison of the named interfaces; feature counts are illustrative.
